# Core Graphics full-coverage layer oracle

The 7,776 rows in `core-graphics-full-coverage.json` were captured on an actual
Mac running macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) on 2026-10-07. They contain independent public
Core Graphics results, exclusively from synthetic premultiplied RGBA8 tuples.
The companion Swift program reproduces the matrix. No user image is included.

The matrix has 36 backdrops, 36 sources, opacity 254/255 and 255/255, and Normal,
Multiply and Screen. A separate copy control confirmed all 39 unique input
tuples materialize unchanged; all 72 repeated cases match the earlier opacity
diagnostic. Expected pixels were copied from the received Mac JSON, never
generated by the Windows renderer.

At full coverage, ordinary image-layer Multiply rounds the overlap and the
combined non-overlap independently before adding them, for all four channels.
The general byte formula is:

```
round(dst * src / 255)
  + round((src * (255 - dstAlpha) + dst * (255 - srcAlpha)) / 255)
```

At 254/255 opacity the source first becomes covered RGBA8 and the final sum
rounds once, as in the previous covered-source oracle. These contracts are
scoped to ordinary image-layer draws. Adjustment kernels and stack composition
retain their existing Core Image blend contract.

The CPU and WebGL tests require exact equality to every received result.
This matrix does not replace the original project, native-package, performance,
or complete Phase 7 acceptance gates.
